FINDINGS

1. Medium. The generated-file scanner does not reject the defined shortened forms when they are followed by a hyphen. The comment claims the opposite.

Path: tests/openspec-cli-compatibility.mjs:57-64, especially line 63. Token list at lines 45-50. Comment at lines 58-59. Controls that miss this case at lines 109-116.

Impact: A generated core skill or command can contain /openspec-new-extra, /openspec-continue-extra, /openspec-ff-extra, /openspec-bulk-archive-extra, or /openspec-verify-extra and the positive scan still passes. Those are the shortened forms design.md:115-118 requires to be rejected, and the same paragraph requires suffix variants not to bypass rejection. The canonical forms and all /opsx: forms are rejected with a hyphen suffix. The shortened forms are not. That is a real handoff-detection gap, not a style issue.

Trigger: assertCoreReferences tokenizes with /(?<![\w/-])(?:\/?openspec-[\w-]+|\/opsx:[\w-]+)/g, then strips a leading slash and rejects only an exact forbidden token or a forbidden token plus another hyphen. For /openspec-new-extra the captured token is the whole string. It is not equal to /openspec-new, and /openspec-new-extra.startsWith("/openspec-new-") is false because the forbidden prefix already ends in a hyphen. The same happens for continue, ff, bulk-archive, and verify. /openspec-onboard-extra is rejected only because /openspec-onboard does not already end in a hyphen.

The synthetic control at line 110 inserts ${token}-extra. For token /openspec-new that produces /openspec-new-extra and assert.throws expects failure. That control currently passes, so it does not detect this hole. The real-file mutation at lines 349-353 uses only /openspec-verify-change, which is the canonical form and does not exercise the short-form hyphen case.

Minimal correction: after normalizing the leading slash, reject when the token equals a forbidden reference or continues with a non-word boundary, including another hyphen. Do not special-case only ${forbidden}-. Add one control per shortened token for ${token}-extra and ${token}-change, on both surfaces, and keep the existing exact, fenced, punctuation, and unrelated-suffix controls. /openspec-newish and /opsx:verifyish must remain accepted.

I did not execute the probe. This is from reading the frozen function. The historical generated files do not contain these short hyphenated forms, so the recorded gate pass does not exercise the hole.

No other product defect found.

Harmless core slash commands and CLI prose such as openspec new change are accepted. The in-memory mutation reads the generated bytes back and checks they were not written.

The init stdout explicitly says the six optional workflows were not installed. The inventory JSON lists exactly the six expected skills, commands, and files. Upstream .gitkeep files under openspec/ are outside the Claude scan and are not the required generated skill/command inventory.

No new spec, dependency, install route, or version policy is in this delta. skip_specs remains true. All six task checkboxes are checked at this head. Plan-time unapproved prose is historical and was not treated as a defect. Approval is the separate exact-plan-approval record, approved true, bound to the same plan and digest.

R4b gates 1-6: command, cwd, start, end, stdout, stderr, and exit. All six exits are 0. Commands match the required six. Cwd is the historical B workspace, a label, not a path executed here. Gate 1 stdout shows the core inventory and the pre-existing metadata/task/archive pass. Its stderr is only an npm update notice. Gate 2 stdout ends at tests 259, pass 259, fail 0, skipped 0. Gate 3 builds 5 skills and 2 plugins. Gate 4 metadata ok true and includes this change's proposal, design, and tasks. Gate 5 native strict JSON has 3 passed and 0 failed, with only the expected skip_specs INFO. Gate 6 is retained-base..head git diff --check, exit 0, empty output.

Candidate helper command binds base, head, plan, and digest. Exit 0. stdout is ok true, tasksComplete true, and the expected tree. stderr empty.

Probe log, core inventory, all 12 generated Claude files, core config, and the two .gitkeep files were read. Probe log records version 1.16.0, the core init, and the later metadata/archive commands with status 0 except the intentional strict-validation negative at status 1.

R4a: local merge stopped before commit, exit 0; merge commit exit 0 naming 9ca1f41; after-head stdout is that same SHA, exit 0; fetch and import-commit exits are 0. Protected planning and probe paths are listed as preserved. R4a result itself says no gates were run there, which is correct: successor gates are R4b.

Scope: target and R3 product-disjoint commands are exact probe diffs and both exits are 0 with empty stdout. Current and resume owner captures were read.
